## Project rules for coding agents (chipgraph)

These rules come from this repository's chipgraph profile and the organization rules it
extends. Follow them whenever you add or change a file.

### Project and blocks

- Project: `qsoc`
- Chip spec: `util/qsoc_contract.yml` (format `qsoc-contract`)
- Target: asic

Each block is an IP. Its instances are the names the chip's memory map uses for it; a
block with no instances listed matches the instance of the same name.

| Block | Instances |
|---|---|
| `bus` | - |
| `common` | - |
| `cpu` | - |
| `dma` | `dma_cfg` |
| `dsram` | - |
| `gpio` | `gpio_0`, `gpio_1`, `gpio_2` |
| `i2c` | - |
| `intmap` | - |
| `iomux` | - |
| `isram` | `isram`, `isram_dbg` |
| `pwm` | - |
| `rom` | - |
| `scrc` | - |
| `spi` | `spi`, `spi_device`, `spi_host` |
| `syscsr` | - |
| `sysdbg` | - |
| `timer` | `timer_0`, `timer_1` |
| `top` | - |
| `uart` | `uart_0`, `uart_1` |
| `wdt` | `wdt`, `wdt_wakeup` |

### Where files go

Create each kind of file only at the path its template gives; do not invent new
directories. In a template, `{block}` is the block name and `{BLOCK}` is the block name in upper case.

| Kind | Path template |
|---|---|
| filelist | `design/{block}/{block}.f` |
| spec | `doc/specs/QNSC_{BLOCK}_MAS.md` |

Per-block overrides:

| Block | Kind | Path template |
|---|---|---|
| `dsram` | spec | (none) |
| `intmap` | spec | `doc/specs/QNSC_Interrupt_Map_MAS.md` |
| `isram` | spec | `doc/specs/QNSC_RAM_MAS.md` |
| `rom` | spec | `doc/specs/QNSC_ROM_MAS.md`, `doc/specs/QNSC_BOOT_SPEC.md` |

### Before you open a PR

Run these from the repository root and fix what they report:

```sh
chipgraph ingest    # build the Design Model; the cross checks read it
chipgraph check     # run every configured check; exits 1 if one fails
chipgraph audit     # every finding, grouped by layer
```

Scope a run with `chipgraph check --block <block>` or `chipgraph check --only <check>`.
`chipgraph ingest --strict` and `chipgraph audit --strict` also exit 1, on an error-level
ingest issue or a blocking finding.

Configured checks (a severity caps what the check reports; a command's `{block}` is the
block name):

| Check | Adapter | Severity | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cdc_struct` | cdc_struct | - | - |
| `connect` | connect | - | - |
| `contract_tags` | cmd | - | `make contract-tags BLOCK={block}` |
| `cross_chip` | cross_chip | - | - |
| `duplicate` | duplicate | - | - |
| `hardcode` | hardcode | - | - |
| `lint` | cmd | - | `make lint BLOCK={block}` |
| `module_rules` | cmd | - | `make module-rules BLOCK={block}` |
| `naming` | cmd | - | `make naming BLOCK={block}` |
| `ports_diff` | ports_diff | - | - |
| `spec_schema` | spec_schema | - | - |
| `trace` | trace | warning | - |

### Requirement IDs

- A requirement ID in a spec must match `{BLOCK}_\d{3}`, with `{block}`/`{BLOCK}` replaced by the block name in lower/upper case (for `bus`: `BUS_\d{3}`).
- Name the ID in the test that covers it: the `trace` check traces each requirement to a test.
- A spec without IDs is read in a temporary mode: each numbered item of its "Verification" section counts as one requirement, keyed by block and content hash. A declared ID always wins; add IDs rather than rely on this.

Per-block overrides:

| Block | ID pattern | Inferred from "Verification" |
|---|---|---|
| `rom` | `(?:ROM\|BOOT)_\d{3}` | yes |
| `scrc` | `SCRC_[A-Z]+_\d{3}` | yes |

### Path exceptions

These paths follow different rules. Do not write under a path whose write is `deny`,
and do not add a new exception without a reason the reviewer accepts.

| Path | Block | Checks | Write | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `doc/specs/QNSC_TEMPLATE_MAS.md` | - | ingest off | allow | the team's MAS template, not the spec of a block |
